title: The Nightingale
summary: A rich man keeps a singing bird until a strange metal bird arrives.
coverScene: A tiny real bird sits on a large green leaf next to a shining golden mechanical toy under the soft moon.

sentences.text: In an era long since surrendered to the mists of history, the sovereign of a magnificent realm inhabited a palace constructed from the purest white stone.
This architectural marvel commanded the admiration of the entire world, primarily because it boasted a legendary garden filled with botanical wonders.
Vibrant blossoms unfurled their petals across immaculate lawns, creating a tapestry of fragrance that captivated every visitor who passed through the towering gates.
The magnificent garden did not merely terminate at the palace walls; rather, it extended deep into the ancient embrace of a shadowy, formidable forest.
Within the mysterious depths of those darkening woods, a tiny, unassuming creature found its home and sang melodies of incomparable sweetness.
Every single night, as twilight surrendered to the velvet mantle of darkness, the little bird would pour forth a cascade of pure, resonant notes.
Travelers, scholars, and monarchs from distant corners of the globe journeyed to the imperial capital for the sole purpose of hearing this legendary song.
They stood in hushed reverence beneath the canopy of trees, marveling at how such an insignificant form could produce music of such profound emotional resonance.
It was inevitable that word of this auditory marvel would eventually reach the supreme ruler through the royal chronicles and official documents of his own domain.
Intrigued by what he read regarding the feathered musician, the sovereign commanded his highest-ranking officers to locate and secure the creature immediately.
The royal entourage scoured the forest until they finally discovered the modest brown bird perched upon a mossy branch, pouring its heart into the evening air.
They brought the trembling little creature back to the gleaming palace, presenting it to the sovereign as if it were a rare jewel plundered from an exotic land.
Moved by curiosity and a desire for exclusive ownership, the ruler commanded that the animal be placed in a miniature cage fashioned entirely from solid gold.
When the guards opened the tiny door and urged the bird to sing for the court, the creature opened its beak and produced a melody so poignant.
The song was so exquisite and filled with such delicate longing that the powerful ruler found himself weeping tears of pure, unexpected happiness.
Despite the opulent surroundings and the lavish attention of the court, the little bird experienced a profound sense of imprisonment within its golden confines.
It longed desperately to spread its weary wings and soar back to the familiar, whispering green trees of the dark forest where it was born.
Day after day, the bird remained trapped inside the gleaming cage, its glorious songs gradually tinged with a subtle undertone of captive sorrow.
The courtiers, however, were entirely consumed by the novelty of their prize, paying little heed to the obvious distress of their captive guest.
They believed that a golden prison was sufficient compensation for the loss of freedom, provided the music continued to flow without interruption.
The status quo of the imperial court shifted dramatically upon the arrival of an ornate package sent by a neighboring monarch of great wealth.
Inside the velvet-lined box rested a mechanical masterpiece: an artificial bird completely covered in gleaming gold and encrusted with precious diamonds and rubies.
This ingenious invention possessed a complex internal mechanism that allowed it to sing a delightful melody whenever someone wound it up with a tiny key.
While the courtiers and the sovereign were distracted by the dazzling display of craftsmanship and the mechanical song, the real bird slipped away.
Taking advantage of an open window and the general preoccupation of the guards, the little creature flew out into the open sky and returned to the forest.
Not a single person in the crowded hall noticed the quiet departure of the living bird, so completely mesmerized were they by the glittering newcomer.
The imperial court embraced the mechanical substitute with immense enthusiasm, delighted by the fact that it could perform the exact same tune repeatedly.
Every noble and advisor declared that the artificial creation was far superior to the unpredictable and fragile creature of flesh and blood.
After all, the machine never grew tired, never demanded freedom, and unfailingly delivered the identical performance whenever its tiny golden key was turned.
For months and years, the court basked in the comforting predictability of the mechanical song, content in their golden illusion of perfection.
Several years drifted past in a predictable rhythm, until the complex internal gears of the mechanical bird began to grind and stall.
The delicate springs inside the golden body wore down from endless repetition, and the intricate music sputtered to a sudden, permanent halt.
When the royal watchmakers examined the device, they shook their heads solemnly and declared that the internal damage was completely irreparable.
Simultaneously, the aging sovereign fell into a severe decline, his body growing progressively weaker, colder, and more fragile with each passing day.
He lay upon his grand imperial bed beneath heavy silk sheets, struggling to draw breath while oppressive shadows gathered in the corners of the vast bedchamber.
A heavy silence settled over the gloomy room, broken only by the labored breathing of the dying ruler who stared blankly at the ceiling.
The silent, broken machine rested uselessly upon a nearby table, serving as a bitter reminder of the fragility of human artifice and ambition.
As the sovereign looked into the gathering darkness, he realized with terrifying clarity that the cold specter of death was sitting quietly beside his bed.
Desperate for comfort, the frail ruler whispered a feeble request for music, hoping that some melody might drive away the creeping chill.
Yet the golden machine remained mute on its stand, unable to offer a single note to soothe the troubled spirit of the failing monarch.
Just as despair threatened to consume the final remnants of his life, a magnificent, unexpected sound drifted softly in through the open window.
Perched gracefully upon a familiar branch outside, the real nightingale was pouring forth a cascade of notes more radiant than any heard before.
The sweet, unadorned music flooded the royal chamber, acting as an invisible shield that slowly drove away the dark shadow of death.
Color began to return to the pale cheeks of the ruler as the powerful vitality of the forest song washed over his weary frame.
With a surge of renewed strength, the sovereign sat up in his bed and thanked the little animal with every ounce of his grateful heart.
The little bird listened to the ruler's words of gratitude and offered a solemn promise to return to the palace gardens every single night.
It vowed to sing of everything happening across the vast empire, bringing news of both the humble peasants and the mighty lords.
The sovereign acknowledged that if he had truly listened to the living bird in the past, he would have avoided much needless sorrow.
He also understood that his own carelessness had driven the creature away, and he marveled at the boundless forgiveness of the tiny singer.
The triumphant song of the returned nightingale echoed across the palace grounds, bringing immense joy and lasting peace to the entire country.
